A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched across the changed pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated linear-bandit experiments, including cumulative regret and suboptimality comparisons in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original linear-bandit results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including Figures 3–7.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, supervised objective, scheduler, and restart procedure remain unchanged. The main-text indexing correction aligns the description with the zero-indexed construction already present in v1 Appendix E.1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic linear-bandit tasks: low non-stationarity with elevated-reward intervals and oscillating high non-stationarity, including evaluation at b = 0.018 and 0.025.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain LinUCB, Thompson Sampling, MASTER+LinUCB, and MASTER+TS. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same data generation, training samples, reward settings, baseline hyperparameters, and metrics. Both use d = 32, 10 actions, 1,000/200 evaluation rounds, and a 16-layer, 16-head GPT-2 trained for 200 epochs.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same suboptimality analyses and the b = 0.025 generalization failure case. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions describe the shading in Figures 3–7 as standard deviations. There are no added run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 3–7 reuse identical empirical plot images, with unchanged curves, rankings, and uncertainty bands. The accompanying findings, including weaker transformer performance at b = 0.025, are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the starting index from i = 1 to i = 0 in the sigma1 concatenation and sigma2 input family, correcting their inconsistency with the stated n+1 copies and Appendix E.1. The assumptions, regret bounds, and appendix proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about nearly optimal dynamic regret, transformer approximation of non-stationarity-handling strategies, and empirical performance matching or sometimes exceeding expert algorithms.

C2.justification: The assumption justification and limitations in Appendix A are already present in v1. Both retain the standard-transformer proof discussion and attribute difficulty at b = 0.025 to limited training coverage of highly non-stationary scenarios.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures, synthetic-data specifications, training budget, and baseline hyperparameters in Section 5 and Appendix B are unchanged. No code/data-access, hardware, or runtime information is added.

R1.justification: The sliding-window Thompson-sampling citation changes from Fiandri et al. (2024) to Trovo et al. (2020) in Section 4.1 and Appendix E.4. Other reference edits largely update bibliographic metadata; the overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Appendix A cross-reference and acknowledgements, expands author affiliation/contact information, and edits bibliography presentation. The substantive prose and section/appendix organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference-template typography and title formatting, with resized and relocated displays. Figure 2 reverses the order-axis direction and moves the time axis above the diagram; Algorithm 2 separates initialization and loop lines. The table and empirical panels are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the scheduler indexing to agree with the existing appendix construction and fixes Figure 2's order-axis direction, reducing inconsistencies in the method description. The added assumption cross-reference improves navigation. These are limited clarity gains; the theoretical guarantees, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
